title_en: Decision of the Supreme People's Court on Amending the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Trial of Cases by the Circuit Courts

articles.content_en:
Article 1 The Supreme People's Court shall establish circuit courts to accept relevant cases within circuit areas. The First Circuit Court shall be located in Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province, with a circuit area covering the four provinces and autonomous regions of Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, and Hunan. The Second Circuit Court shall be located in Shenyang City, Liaoning Province, with a circuit area covering the three provinces of Liaoning, Jilin, and Heilongjiang. The Third Circuit Court shall be located in Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province, with a circuit area covering the five provinces and municipalities of Jiangsu, Shanghai, Zhejiang, Fujian, and Jiangxi. The Fourth Circuit Court shall be located in Zhengzhou City, Henan Province, with a circuit area covering the four provinces of Henan, Shanxi, Hubei, and Anhui. The Fifth Circuit Court shall be located in Chongqing City, with a circuit area covering the five provinces, autonomous regions, and municipality of Chongqing, Sichuan, Guizhou, Yunnan, and Tibet. The Sixth Circuit Court shall be located in Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province, with a circuit area covering the five provinces and autonomous regions of Shaanxi, Gansu, Qinghai, Ningxia, and Xinjiang. The headquarters of the Supreme People's Court shall directly accept cases concerning the five provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities of Beijing, Tianjin, Hebei, Shandong, and Inner Mongolia.
The Supreme People's Court may, according to relevant provisions and the needs of adjudication work, add circuit courts and adjust the circuit areas and scope of case acceptance of the circuit courts.

Article 2 A circuit court shall be a permanent adjudication institution dispatched by the Supreme People's Court. The judgments, rulings, and decisions rendered by a circuit court shall be the judgments, rulings, and decisions of the Supreme People's Court.

Article 4 Cases involving intellectual property, foreign-related commercial matters, maritime affairs, death penalty review, state compensation, enforcement, and protests by the Supreme People's Procuratorate shall temporarily be tried or handled by the headquarters of the Supreme People's Court.

Article 5 A circuit court shall establish a litigation service center to receive and register case materials within the scope of case acceptance of the circuit court, and to provide litigation services to the parties. For materials of cases that shall be accepted by the headquarters of the Supreme People's Court in accordance with these Provisions, if a party requests that the circuit court forward them, the circuit court shall forward them.
A circuit court shall, for cases that meet the case-filing conditions, uniformly assign case numbers and file cases on the Supreme People's Court case-handling information platform.

Article 6 Where a party disagrees with a first-instance administrative or civil/commercial judgment or ruling rendered by a Higher People's Court within the circuit area and files an appeal, the petition of appeal shall be submitted to the circuit court through the original trial People's Court. If a party directly appeals to the circuit court, the circuit court shall, within five days, transfer the petition of appeal to the original trial People's Court. The original trial People's Court, upon receiving the petition of appeal and the statement of defense, shall, within five days, submit them together with all case files and evidence to the circuit court.

Article 7 Where a party files an application for retrial or a petition against a legally effective judgment or ruling rendered by a Higher People's Court within the circuit area, the party shall submit the application for retrial, petition, and other materials to the circuit court.

Article 8 Where the Supreme People's Court considers that a case accepted by a circuit court has significant guiding significance for the uniform application of law, it may decide that the case shall be tried by its headquarters.
Where a circuit court considers that a case it has already accepted has significant guiding significance for the uniform application of law, it may report to the headquarters of the Supreme People's Court for trial.
Article 9 A circuit court may, based on the needs of adjudication work, conduct circuit trials of cases and receive visitors within the circuit area.

Article 10 A circuit court shall, in accordance with the principle of letting the trial judge adjudicate and the adjudicator bear responsibility, implement the responsibility system for case handling by the presiding judge and the collegial panel. The presiding judges of a circuit court shall be selected by the Supreme People's Court from among judicial personnel with outstanding case-handling capabilities and rich trial experience. The collegial panel of a circuit court shall be composed of presiding judges.

Article 11 The chief judge and deputy chief judges of a circuit court shall participate in the collegial panel to try cases. When the collegial panel tries a case, the presiding judge handling the case shall serve as the chief judge. When the chief judge or a deputy chief judge participates in the collegial panel to try a case, he or she shall serve as the chief judge. The judgments and rulings rendered by a circuit court shall, after being signed by the members of the collegial panel, be issued by the chief judge.

Article 12 Cases accepted by a circuit court shall be uniformly incorporated into the comprehensive management platform for trial information of the Supreme People's Court for management, and the case-filing information, trial procedures, and judgment documents shall be disclosed to the parties and the public according to law.

Article 13 A circuit court shall establish an integrity supervisor responsible for the daily integrity supervision work of the circuit court.
The Supervision Bureau of the Supreme People's Court shall conduct integrity supervision over the circuit court and its staff members by accepting reports and complaints, investigating and handling disciplinary cases, conducting judicial inspections, and carrying out judicial affairs supervision.
